svg.metadata: {"device_model":{"id":"elab.hobbyist-devices.v1","pwm":"Generic powered PWM clock: configurable 10..1000 Hz and 10..90 percent duty. Rise/fall each occupy 5 percent of a period. Duty includes the rising phase. Output uses complementary 50 ohm paths, 1 Gohm off bleed, 1 Mohm supply load and smooth supply enable from 2 to 3 V. No feedback compensation, current limit, temporal dead time, switching loss, noise or hardware rating. Buck examples simulate external switched power stages, not an averaged converter.","opamp_dynamics":"Optional dominant-pole and slew-limited compensation for the unchanged generic op-amp output stage. Gain-bandwidth and slew rate are saved settings; a private 1 nF compensation capacitor charges from the modeled rails, preserving KCL, energy and explicit dissipation. The output target remains bounded by the present rails even when stored compensation voltage outlasts a falling supply. Existing op-amps without dynamics retain their original equations. No fitted silicon identity, noise, offset, multiple poles, protection or thermal ratings.","shift_register":"Generic 8-bit serial-in parallel-out register with separate positive-edge shift and output-latch clocks, active-low shift clear, active-low parallel output enable, and serial cascade output independent of output enable. State starts cleared; power loss clears both registers. Sixteen internal D memories reuse sequential-v1 edge/guard laws; internal data uses ideal logic rails with explicit 1 Gohm loading, while finite 50 ohm drive is applied only at public Q/SERIAL outputs. A logic-v1 inverter maps active-low clear. Simultaneous shift/latch/cascade clocks sample pre-edge data. Parallel buffers use 50 ohm paths when enabled and 1 Gohm to their selected rail when disabled; OE interpolates across the declared 30/70 percent input interval. Serial has its own 50 ohm buffer. No package pinout, propagation or setup/hold timing, metastability, current/thermal ratings.","sound":"Generic capacitive piezo sounder and DC-powered active buzzer. Passive piezo uses explicit capacitance and leakage; acoustic preview is a normalized illustrative terminal-voltage signal, not calibrated SPL or a mechanical/room simulation. Active buzzer uses a passive voltage-dependent DC load and an ideal acoustic oscillator; no electrical oscillator ripple. Opening or simulating a project never plays audio. Preview rendering, playback, stopping and WAV export are explicit shared commands."},"diode_model":{"id":"elab.generic-silicon-diode.v1","is_a":1e-9,"n":1.7,"rs_ohm":1,"temperature_c":27,"limitations":"Generic silicon junction with Shockley forward/reverse leakage and
